source.author: muser
source.notes: Plasma is an open-source (GPL) dual-stage distortion with sculpting filters. Signal flow: Pre Gain → highpass / peak / dual peak / lowpass filters → Distortion (Drive, Type, Girth, Bias) → Late Distortion (second stage) → Gain → Mix. Use it as an effect: {"type": "plugin", "path": "~/.vst3/Plasma.vst3", "params": {...}}. All 29 parameters are on a 0–1 scale; write the text the plugin displays ("4.00", "150.0", "Soft Clip") instead of guessing numbers.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Amount of distortion, 1.00 (none) to 11.00. The default 1.00 leaves the sound almost clean. 2–3 = warm saturation, 4–6 = obvious grit, 8+ = heavy

params.name: Distortion Type
params.description: Shape of the first stage. Soft Clip / Saturate = warm, musical; Hard Clip = tight, aggressive; Atan / Crunch = bright grit; Bitcrush = lo-fi digital; Sine / Cosine / Harmonic = wavefolding, synthetic overtones; Scream / Extreme / Weird = sound design

params.name: Girth
params.description: Adds noisy, fizzy grit on top of the distortion. 0.00 = clean distortion; any value away from 0 (either sign) brightens a lot. Keep within ±0.3 for musical parts

params.name: Bias
params.description: Asymmetry of the distortion curve: away from 0 adds even harmonics (tube-like warmth, a bit of 'growl'). ±0.2–0.5 is typical

params.name: Pre Gain
params.description: Input level into the filters and distortion, -32.0 to +32.0 dB (default 0.0). Raising it drives the distortion harder, like Drive

params.name: Highpass Freq
params.description: Highpass before the distortion, in Hz (default 20.0 = off). 100–300 keeps the low end from turning to mud: the distortion then works only on mids and highs

params.name: Lowpass Freq
params.description: Lowpass before the distortion, in Hz (default 20000.0 = off). Lower it to distort a darker signal (fewer harsh highs)

params.name: Peak Freq
params.description: Centre of the peak EQ before the distortion, in Hz (default 450.0). Boosting a band here makes that band distort first

params.name: Peak Gain
params.description: Peak EQ gain, -48.0 to +48.0 dB (default 0.0). +6 to +12 dB at 1000–2500 Hz = more bite

params.name: Late Drive
params.description: Drive of the second distortion stage (after the first), 1.00 = off. Stacking two mild stages (e.g. 3.00 + 3.00) is thicker than one heavy stage

params.name: Late Distortion Type
params.description: Shape of the second stage; same choices as Distortion Type

params.name: Gain
params.description: Output level, -32.0 to +32.0 dB (default 0.0), applied after Mix (to dry and wet). Use it to level-match: usually -3 to -8 dB at high Drive, +1 to +3 dB for low Mix with a highpassed wet path. Never push it far above 0

params.name: Mix
params.description: Dry/wet crossfade in percent (default 100.00). 20–40 = parallel distortion: keeps the clean transient and adds grit underneath. 0.00 is exactly the dry signal

presets.name: warm
presets.description: Gentle saturation: thickens bass, keys and vocals without obvious distortion

presets.name: bass_grit
presets.description: Adds upper-harmonic grit to a bass so it cuts through; the highpassed wet path leaves the sub to the dry signal

presets.name: drum_crush
presets.description: Parallel drum-bus crunch: punchier, more aggressive drums

presets.name: scream
presets.description: Two-stage heavy distortion for leads and sound design

tips: The output is clipped at about -3 dBFS: as soon as Drive or Pre Gain pushes the signal up, the peak sits at -3 dBFS and only the density (RMS/LUFS) grows. Judge distortion by loudness and brightness, not peak.
Distortion makes things much louder (+5 to +9 LUFS at Drive 4–11). Level-match with Gain (output) so the A/B comparison is fair and the mix doesn't jump.
On bass, put a highpass (150–250 Hz) before the drive and use Mix 25–40 %. Mix is a crossfade, so the dry sub drops a little (about -3 dB at 30 %): add 1–3 dB of Gain to compensate.
Girth adds a lot of fizz even at small values; leave it at 0.00 unless you want noise.
Bitcrush, Harmonic and Scream are quieter than the clip types at the same Drive; Atan, Crunch and Weird are much brighter.
Mix 0.00 is exactly the dry signal, so Mix can be automated for a distortion fade-in.
Continuous parameters display plain numbers. In `muser audition --values`, wrap them in double quotes so they are sent as text: --values '"2.00","4.00"'.
